name: Palazzo Chiericati

dates.altered: Bought by the city in 1838-39, restored, and opened as a museum in 1855.
dates.note: The consortium's page dates the design: 'of 1550, the year Palladio gave the designs to Girolamo Chiericati'. The node's exemplar note gives 'Begun 1550, completed only in 1680'; nothing read here bears on the completion date.

quotes.text: The piece of architecture which adds dignity to the Piazza is the Palazzo Chiericati, of 1550, the year Palladio gave the designs to Girolamo Chiericati. It is the most spectacular civilian residence designed by Palladio, today seat of the Vicenza Town Museum. It was purchased in 1838-39, then renovated and finally turned into a museum and opened in 1855.

note: Tranche 3, the antique orders cluster, 5 Sep 2026. The register calls it 'the most spectacular civilian residence designed by Palladio' and says nothing whatever about the two-storey open loggia across the whole front, which is the ONLY reason this node names the building. Its own text is one paragraph long; the survey is that paragraph.
